The '''Q7-series astromech droid''' was an experimental [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]], designed specifically for use in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Vwing_ICS.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A spherical Q7-series in a V-wing starfighter.]]

Unlike the [[R-series/Legends|R-series]], the Q7-series droids were spherical. The upper hemisphere contained the regular dome, while the lower hemisphere housed [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] engines which allowed the Q7 to get itself in and out of a V-wing fighter, as well as taking up less space while jacked into the fighter itself.

[[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] designed several prototypes, labeled Q1 through Q6, before finally producing the Q7. They based the upper dome on the [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series]], both to save money on production and due to the success of the largely popular R2-series. This was where the similarities ended, as the lower part of the droid was another dome making the droid under 1 meter in diameter.

Problems arose with the Q7s, due to the frequency in which their repulsorlifts broke down, more often than the treads of their larger cousins in the R-series line. It was also more expensive to repair a repulsorlift engine than the more simple treads. The Q7 also lacked any kind of back-up option for locomotion, rendering them useless if their repulsorlifts did fail.

==History==
As the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was transformed into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and the V-wing was replaced by the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] starfighter in the Imperial military, Q7 astromechs were phased out and production ceased on the line. In the decades before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] many Q7s found their way into the hands of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and merchants in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Due to the higher cost of repairing the repulsorlifts, many owners abandoned their droids for easier-to-maintain models. Other Q7s were converted to [[R2]] models or [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4]] models, and still others had their programming and personality transferred into completely different droid models.

By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it was rare to see a Q7 in its original form.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Q7-series_astromech.jpg|thumb|right|The incorrect portrayal of a Q7-series astromech droid. It is actually an R7 astromech droid.]]
A Q7-series droid was accidentally called an '[[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4]] series droid' in the [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] set 6205 V-wing Fighter.

The image for the Q7 in ''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]'' contradicts the description of the droid as being a hovering, spherical droid. It appears to depict an [[R7-series astromech droid|R7]]-series astromech with its distinctive triangular sensor, as opposed to the rounded sensor the Q7 borrows from the R2 unit.
